s: a gilded Belle Époque dining hall built into a working train station since 1901
w: Built for the 1900 Exposition Universelle and opened in 1901, this first-floor dining room inside Gare de Lyon is pure fin-de-siècle theatre: soaring ceilings, gilt moulding, and 41 monumental paintings of the old PLM railway's destinations across France. Classic brasserie cooking -- escargots, foie gras, a proper roast -- plays second fiddle to the room itself, but both hold up. A Paris rite of passage as much as a meal.
_facts: Located on the first floor of Gare de Lyon, Place Louis Armand, 75012 Paris
Opened in 1901 for the 1900 Exposition Universelle, built by the PLM railway company
Decorated with 41 large paintings depicting destinations along the former PLM network
Listed as a French historic monument (monument historique) since 1972

s: a Paris restaurant that has served only soufflés, savoury and sweet, since 1961
w: Founded in 1961 by Claude Rigaud on the single, slightly eccentric idea of a menu built entirely from soufflés -- cheese or foie gras to start, a Grand Marnier soufflé to finish, nothing else on offer that isn't puffed and baked to order. White-jacketed service and a retro dining room between Place Vendôme and the Madeleine haven't changed in six decades, and neither has the devotion of its regulars.
_facts: Located at 36 Rue du Mont Thabor, 75001 Paris, near Place Vendôme
Founded in 1961 by Claude Rigaud around a single-dish concept: soufflés only
Menu covers savoury soufflés (cheese, foie gras, seafood) through to sweet dessert soufflés
The Grand Marnier soufflé is the house's best-known dish

s: a three-Michelin-star Place des Vosges dining room run on classical technique since 1986
w: Bernard Pacaud's restaurant has held three Michelin stars for decades from a single elegant room under the arcades of Place des Vosges. The cooking is deliberately classical -- no trend-chasing, no tasting-menu theatre -- built on flawless sauce work and dishes like the langoustine ravioli that have anchored the menu for years. Notoriously hard to book, it draws a devoted international following that treats a table here as a pilgrimage.
_facts: Located at 9 Place des Vosges, 75004 Paris
Run by chef Bernard Pacaud since opening in 1986 (moved to this address in 1986)
Known for classical French technique, including its long-running langoustine ravioli
